summary: Wang Xizhi's illness plea, resignation from Kuaiji, and tomb-side oath are his own events, dated in the chapter to 東晉穆帝永和十一年三月癸卯朔九日辛亥. That ganzhi pair matches the third month of Yonghe 11. The conventional Western year of Yonghe 11 is AD 355; the dated day falls in AD 355 on both the Julian table (355-04-07) and proleptic Gregorian (355-04-06). A later 告誓文 anecdote that reads 永和十年 is calendrically incompatible with 癸卯朔 and does not override the chapter. Several other dated rows do not survive. s0156 never says 永和十一年; Wang Shu's Yang appointment is narratively earlier than the oath, and 晉書穆帝紀 places it in 永和十年二月 (AD 354). Tan is only named in a comparison, not as an actor in 355. 夙遭閔凶 and 母兄鞠育 do not yield an AD 317–345 activity window; that span is an Eastern-Jin dynasty bracket, not uncertainty about one event. 于父母墓前 shows both parents already dead by the oath, so the mother's death is omitted while the father's early death is otherwise attested. 老氏 and 周任 are retrospective citations inside the 355 oath, not Spring-and-Autumn or Western-Zhou life dates. 羲之既去官, the Xu Mai travels, and Xie An's 嘗謂 remark are one-sided after the resignation, not an exact AD 355 year, and they must not feed living activity hints.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi dated his own tomb-side resignation oath to Yonghe 11.3.9.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event belongs to Wang Xizhi (p035), who names himself 小子羲之 while swearing before his parents' tombs. The Chinese day is explicit: 東晉穆帝司馬聃, era 永和, year 11, month 3, first day 癸卯, ninth day 辛亥. The stem-branch arithmetic is internally consistent (癸卯 plus eight days is 辛亥). Wikipedia's 永和(東晉) month table, which follows the pre-1582 Julian convention also used by Academia Sinica, gives that first day as Julian 355-03-30, so day 9 is Julian 355-04-07. One day earlier in proleptic Gregorian (355-04-06) still lies in AD 355; the year-precision westernYear is therefore justified and does not require a second invented endpoint. A later 太平廣記/國史異纂 reception of the 告誓文 reads 永和十年三月癸卯, but 永和十年三月 is 戊申朔 on the same table, so that variant cannot carry the oath's own 癸卯朔. The chapter reading 十一年 stands. Conventional regnal-year 355 equals the Gregorian year of this third-month day.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi's undated travels and conversations after he had already left office.
itemChecks.reason: 羲之既去官 is a one-sided bound after the Yonghe 11.3.9 resignation, not a second exact-year event. The owner of the only calendar date is still Xizhi's oath; s0173–s0175 and s0178 then narrate roaming, the Xu Mai herb journeys, Xie An's 嘗謂 remark, and the court's later refusal to recall him. Those are subsequent and open-ended. Turning the bound into westernYear AD 355 with certainty explicit invents a false endpoint and then uses that year as if the later anecdotes were dated. Keep 既去官 as after/onOrAfter the oath; do not assign the whole retirement dossier to 355.
